summary: A note from BBN after an IMP software update added a delay of about 30 seconds before the IMP accepted messages from a host that had just come up. Some host programs had timeouts that treated this as a failure and shut down. BBN asked that BBN Report 1822 be treated as the fixed, authoritative description of the host-IMP interface.

plainLanguage.summary: An IMP update added a delay before it accepted messages from a host that had just come alive. Some host programs timed out and shut down, so BBN asked sites to follow the written interface specification.

subtitle: BBN explains why hosts should follow the documented IMP interface.

tldr.problem: A new IMP version introduced a startup delay that caused some NCPs to treat the IMP as failed and shut down.
tldr.mechanism: BBN urges hosts to rely only on behavior guaranteed by BBN Report 1822 and report problems instead of relying on undocumented behavior.
tldr.outcome: BBN was preparing an update to Report 1822 and considering interface features for version detection and host status.

today: RFC 209 is an IMP/Host interface notice published in August 1971. The unit metadata lists its status as Unknown.

sections.title: The Startup Delay Problem
sections.content:
IMP system version 2500 corrected a problem that caused hosts to receive spurious Destination Dead messages. The correction made the IMP refuse host messages for about 30 seconds after the host indicated it was coming alive.

Some NCPs had shorter limits for how long an IMP could take to accept a message. When the delay exceeded those limits, the NCP declared the IMP inoperative and shut itself down.
sections.plainLanguage: A change intended to stop false failure messages caused some host programs to time out. They shut down before the IMP's new waiting period ended.

sections.title: Use the Documented Interface
sections.content:
BBN said the change did not alter an advertised system property, but acknowledged the trouble it caused. To prevent similar misunderstandings, it argued that the IMP/Host interface should be documented, understood and stable.

BBN asked hosts to assume that features not specifically guaranteed by BBN Report 1822 do not exist. It advised sites to report problems to BBN rather than work around them or infer behavior from experiments.
sections.plainLanguage: Hosts should rely on behavior that the interface document promises. If a problem occurs, BBN asks sites to report it instead of depending on undocumented behavior.

sections.title: Planned Documentation and Features
sections.content: BBN was working on an update to Report 1822 to reflect removal of the cease mechanism described in RFC 107. It was also considering a way for hosts to detect an IMP system version and receive information about which hosts were alive.
sections.plainLanguage: BBN planned to update the interface report. It was also considering ways for hosts to learn the IMP version and network host status.
